- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak sentiment-driven peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts are prone to over-optimism; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply 2–5% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- Avoid forecasting >10% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.80 for 3+ days).
